clue.text: "Parts" I said, "are mixed in the plant"

indicators.note: the quoted speaker's words are mixed, so their letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone, speaking of parts, remarks that they are mixed together in a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are mixed' tells you to rearrange PARTS, I and SAID, all ten letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy Victorian parlour houseplant with broad leaves.

clue.text: Virgil's arms embrace the love that's given by Rose

indicators.note: the arms wrap round the love, holding it inside

parts.note: Arma virumque cano opens Virgil's Aeneid; arma is Latin for arms
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A poet's arms embrace a beloved, a gesture offered by a girl called Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' puts O inside ARMA. Rose is the flower, not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose gives off a fragrance, a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Choir-master bothers Roper about money

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes about the money, enclosing it
bothers suggests the name Roper is troubled and thrown into disorder

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: A choirmaster pesters a man called Roper over cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothers' turns ROPER into PRE + OR, and 'about' wraps that round CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A precentor leads the singing of a church choir or congregation.

clue.text: Fall overboard? Not much!

definitions.meaning: read literally, to plunge over the side of a ship into the sea
a tiny amount, insignificant beside what is needed

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a plunge into the sea; idiomatically an amount too small to matter.

clue.text: One's in hides to see birds

indicators.note: in places the contracted one's inside the word for hides, as if tucked into a birdwatcher's shelter

parts.note: hides are animal skins
one is I, so one's is I'S, contracted to IS

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sits in hides to spot wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is 'one is', I + S. 'hides' looks like birdwatchers' shelters but means SKINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellowish-green finch.

clue.text: Lawrence incognito, deep in the Antarctic

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the alias Ross
the deep is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia, travelling disguised, ends up deep in Antarctica.
explanation.walkthrough: After fame in Arabia, Lawrence joined the RAF as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean on the Antarctic coast.

clue.text: Does a rabbit end in this cutlet?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words this cutlet, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a rabbit's rear finished up in this cutlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run thiS CUTlet, which holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer, its back end.

clue.text: Unfortunately CIA is without public relations in the island

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jumbled agency is outside the PR
unfortunately implies things have gone wrong for the CIA, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly the CIA has no press office on the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. 'Unfortunately' makes CAI of CIA, split round PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Tracts, as it might be between trees

indicators.note: the jumbled pair goes between the letters of trees, splitting the word
might be suggests the words as it could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Pamphlets stuck between trees, as might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' turns AS IT into ATIS, which 'between' sets inside TREES as TRE-ATIS-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a written work dealing formally with a subject, like a tract.

clue.text: No blooming treachery, thus early foiled

definitions.text: No blooming treachery, thus early foiled

parts.words: No blooming treachery, thus early foiled
parts.note: a plot stopped before it can flower, as a gardener pinches off a shoot so it never blossoms

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means checked at an early stage, from pinching off buds before they open.

clue.text: Unity, awfully sour, and burdensome

parts.note: unity is the number one

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word sour is badly mangled, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of three qualities: unity, an awfully sour mood, and a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unity' suggests togetherness, but here it is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Something onerous weighs heavily on you, like a heavy duty or load.

clue.text: Dotty painting of Scott's opening drink

indicators.note: the opening of the word Scott's is its first letter

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A picture painted under the influence of Scott's first drink of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like 'daft', but it means made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is a technique of painting or drawing with many small dots.

clue.text: So be it, one draws pleasant features

parts.note: amen is Hebrew for so be it, said at the end of a prayer
the Roman numeral for one is I
a tie is a drawn game, so draws are ties

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a result philosophically and then sketches the nice parts of a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' is the sporting noun, not the verb for sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are the agreeable facilities or attractions of a place.

clue.text: See 14 ac
Has small French cricketer in stitches

parts.note: petit is French for small
point is a fielding position in cricket, and so the fielder standing there

explanation.surface: A tiny French cricket player is laughing helplessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stitches' suggests helpless laughter, but the stitches are embroidery. POINT is a cricket fielder placed square of the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit point is fine needlework made of small diagonal tent stitches on canvas.

clue.text: Sweets 'e 'id in father's cash-drawers

parts.note: pa is father, so father's is PA'S

indicators.note: Cockney for hid in: the letter is concealed inside the drawers

parts.note: tills are cash drawers in shops
Cockney he, with the h dropped, leaving just E

explanation.surface: A Cockney lad hid sweets in his dad's cash drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h's are Cockney speech: 'e 'id = he hid. 'id in' tucks E inside TILLS after PA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastilles are small chewy or medicated sweets.

clue.text: Ship loaded with fish or fruit

indicators.note: the ship carries the fish inside it like cargo

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the haddock is a North Atlantic food fish

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying a cargo of either fish or fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' sets up a choice of fish or fruit, but the fish sits inside the ship and only the fruit defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is a large citrus fruit, the pomelo, a forerunner of the grapefruit.

clue.text: Agitation in the firm over many a proposal

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Uproar in a company over a great many proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: M for a thousand often stands for 'many' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Commotion is noisy disturbance and agitation.

clue.text: Desire, perhaps, American public transport

definitions.meaning: Tennessee Williams's play is A ... Named Desire, so Desire is an example of one
in the US a tram running on street rails has this name

explanation.surface: A longing for something, perhaps, as against the buses of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire is the named tram in Williams's play, and the word is the US term for a tram.

clue.text: Come detailed to look for an equal

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail cut off, so the word come loses its final letter

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Someone is told in detail to come and seek a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed: COME loses its last letter, E, leaving COM.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is a peer, someone of equal rank or standing.

clue.text: Beats after deserter with these canes!

indicators.note: the beats come after the deserter in the answer

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A deserter is thrashed with canes.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat is a deserter from the saying that rats leave a sinking ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the climbing palm whose stems are made into canes.

clue.text: Anaesthetizes miners — surgeon needed

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers in Britain
BS is Bachelor of Surgery, a surgeon's degree

explanation.surface: Miners trapped underground need a surgeon to put them under.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM, the British miners' trade union, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To anaesthetize a body part is to deaden its feeling, making it insensible.

clue.text: £1 Bill and I make on the side

parts.note: read as one pound: I for one and L for pound, from the Latin libra
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone splits a pound with Bill, earning a little extra on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the side' hints at a sly earning, but it is anatomical: the flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac means relating to the ilium, the hip bone, at the side of the lower trunk.

clue.text: Elgin wild-fire

indicators.note: wild suggests the name Elgin runs out of control, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blaze breaks out in the Scottish town of Elgin.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin is a town in Moray, Scotland; 'wild' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Contest the Oaks perhaps — making it is smashing

parts.note: a match is a sporting contest
oak trees growing together make up a wood

explanation.surface: Entering the Oaks, a famous horse race, and winning it would be marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a classic English flat race for fillies at Epsom; here the oaks are just trees forming a WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: To make splinters of something is to smash it to pieces, matchwood being tiny fragments.

clue.text: Artist tells how to create a vacuum

definitions.meaning: a French Impressionist painter famous for pictures of ballet dancers
read as an instruction: take all the gas out of a vessel

explanation.surface: A painter explains the method for making a vacuum.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is Edgar Degas; split as DE-GAS the name reads as the instruction to remove gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas the Impressionist; and to remove gas leaves a vacuum.

clue.text: Impedimenta for a joke put in a sledge

indicators.note: the joke is placed within the sledge

parts.note: a luge is a small racing sledge
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a joke item on a sledge as baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impedimenta' is Latin for baggage that slows an army down.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta are cumbersome baggage and equipment carried on a journey.

clue.text: Article Dr Heather is moving easily

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a doctor holds an MB, Bachelor of Medicine
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: A doctor named Heather writes an article while strolling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like the doctor's first name, but it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.

clue.text: Part of play heard as well as this

indicators.note: tells us the word spoken is entered as another spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a scene is a division of an act in a play

explanation.surface: Part of a play is to be listened to and watched.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the phrase 'heard as well as seen'; 'this' stands for the answer in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing the stock phrase about being heard and watched, the missing word is the one for being observed.

clue.text: Heads of republics aren't always republicans

definitions.text: Heads of republics aren't always republicans

parts.words: Heads of republics aren't always republicans
parts.note: the leaders of republics may belong to any party, not necessarily the US Republican Party

explanation.definitionFit: The head of state of a republic bears this title, whichever party they come from.
